transcript:
Meeting header
Date: Tue Feb 10 2026 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes (recording auto-start)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Cole (Redwood SE); Diego Marquez (Lumina Tegris, Head of ML); Fiona Zhang (Lumina Tegris, Cloud Architect); Priya Iyer (Lumina Tegris, VP Partnerships)

Summary:
Quick intro between Redwood and Lumina Tegris to explore channel onramp and integration patterns for GPU-enabled cloud partners. Focus areas: routing/latency, dedicated vs hosted model, VPC/private control plane, compliance/KMS, pilot scope and success criteria.

Topics:
- Partner model: reseller vs referral
- Technical integration: API vs direct model onramp, routing, KV cache and batching implications
- Security & compliance: SOC2, customer-managed KMS, data residency
- Pilot plan & success criteria: benchmark latency, cost per token, stability

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samira from Redwood, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer, hey Ethan
[00:07] Ethan Cole: hey all, uh, great to meet you — Diego, Fiona, Priya, thanks for making time
[00:12] Diego Marquez: yep thanks, um, excited to chat, we're looking at partners to help on inference routing for our ML services
[00:18] Fiona Zhang: yep, we've got GPU clusters on GCP and a few edge locations, curious how Redwood would fit in with our channel reseller model
[00:25] Samira Patel: perfect, we'll do a quick framing. objective today: understand Lumina's integration constraints and see if a channel onramp (reseller + managed routing) makes sense. also, figure out next steps — pilot, docs, and contacts
[00:37] [00:38] Priya Iyer: just to add, our timeline is Q2 pilot ideally, procurement in late march, and success is low latencies for gen-heavy features in prod by late q3 — and security is non-negotiable
[00:50] Ethan Cole: got it. quick question on stack — Fiona, you said GCP GPU clusters, anything else? do you use anthos, k8s on prem? what's the network topology
[01:01] Fiona Zhang: mostly GKE with node pools for T4s and some A100s in specific regions; we also have a colo partner for EU edge, which is where data residency comes in
[01:12] Diego Marquez: and we run two main serving patterns — synchronous chat responses (low latency) and batch embedding jobs overnight
[01:19] Ethan Cole: that maps well to Redwood's routing — hosted API for quick POC, dedicated pools for sustained throughput, and private deployments if you need VPC control. question: is tenant data allowed to leave your VPC for a hosted pilot?
[01:32] Fiona Zhang: for pilot maybe, but for production we require customer-managed KMS + VPC peering or private link
[01:40] Samira Patel: understood. our private product supports customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and optional on-prem packages — we'll share the security brief. (note: transcription may mis-parse some acronyms e.g., KMS -> KMS, anthos -> an-thoss)
[01:55] [02:00] Diego Marquez: curious about perf — what's typical p95 for chat at 512 tokens on an A100 vs T4? and how much does batching improve unit cost
[02:10] Ethan Cole: rough numbers off the top: on A100 p95 for autoregressive 512 tokens is sub-200ms per token? hmm, let me be careful — per-request latency depends a lot on batching and kernel selection; we can run a direct baseline on your model binary. batching reduces token cost significantly but adds tail latency when you increase batch windows
[02:28] Diego Marquez: okay yeah we need concrete numbers. also, do you have autoscaling for dedicated pools with burst to hosted when capacity is saturated
[02:36] Samira Patel: yes, we can configure autoscaling policies and fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity — that's one of our reliability differentiators
[02:46] Fiona Zhang: what's the integration footprint — API calls, SDK, or do you mount model artifacts directly in our environment
[02:52] Ethan Cole: typically API first — simple REST + SDKs; for private we offer a control plane and deploy an agent in your VPC which pulls model artifacts, with options for air-gapped on-prem installs
[03:05] [03:10] Priya Iyer: procurement will ask about SLAs, pricing tiers, and channel discounts — do you have partner pricing docs
[03:17] Samira Patel: yes we'll share a partner one-pager and a draft reseller agreement. pricing can be usage-based for hosted and committed monthly for dedicated. discounts for channel partners are standard, we can include a margin table
[03:28] Diego Marquez: question about observability — we need per-tenant token-level cost and tracing across requests, will we get that in a private deployment
[03:36] Ethan Cole: yes, Console supports token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks; for private installs we can ship a metrics collector that exports to your Prometheus/Grafana stack
[03:48] Fiona Zhang: on compliance, we need SOC2 type II and ISO 27001 documentation, and proof of encryption in transit+at rest
[03:55] Samira Patel: we have SOC2 available, ISO in progress, and we support TLS + KMS integrations — will attach the security pack
[04:04] [04:10] Diego Marquez: any red flags with our EU colo? data residency's key; can you guarantee model outputs won't be routed through US regions
[04:18] Ethan Cole: yes, routing policies can be region-bound and we can pin requests to certain model instances; for strict residency we'd recommend private or dedicated with regional capacity
[04:28] Priya Iyer: ok, what's the pilot scope you'd propose for Q2
[04:33] Samira Patel: propose 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding (access + security review), week 1 baseline perf with sample workloads, week 2 integration + tweaks (routing, caching), week 3 soak and reporting; success metrics: <250ms p95 for chat at 512 tokens, stable throughput for 100 req/s, cost per token improvement vs current baseline
[04:53] Diego Marquez: that's reasonable. we'd add an embedding batch run (overnight) and check cost delta vs internal GPU usage
[05:02] Ethan Cole: noted. one more technical note: our runtime supports KV cache and prefix cache which can reduce repeated prompt costs by up to 30% depending on workload
[05:12] Fiona Zhang: how much engineering effort to add Redwood SDK into our service mesh — we use istio and some custom sidecars
[05:19] Ethan Cole: integration is typically minimal — SDK is <200kb, language clients for go/python/java; if you want to do direct connectivity via service mesh, we can provide a sidecar pattern and example helm charts
[05:32] [05:36] Diego Marquez: any legal things specific to partners — indemnity, data processing addendum, do you sign DPAs for EU customers
[05:44] Samira Patel: yes we have standard DPAs and can negotiate specifics; we'll route legal to your procurement. priya, we'll loop in our commercial team
[05:52] Priya Iyer: sounds good. also curious about go-to-market — are there co-sell opportunities or lead sharing
[05:58] Samira Patel: absolutely, channel partners get co-marketing assets and lead sharing for enterprise referrals; details in the partner playbook we'll send
[06:08] [06:15] Ethan Cole: lastly, a perf caveat — if you run very long sequences and use kv cache heavily, we may recommend quantized model variants to keep memory footprint low at the cost of minimal accuracy change
[06:28] Fiona Zhang: do you manage quantization or do we need to provide quantized artifacts
[06:33] Ethan Cole: we support model quantization as part of onboarding and can provide recommendations (8-bit, 4-bit) depending on quality tests
[06:41] Diego Marquez: ok great. any competitors you see in this space we should watch out for
[06:45] Samira Patel: folks often evaluate Aperture AI and CloudForge for managed endpoints, and some partners use NimbleGPU for pure channel resale
[06:55] Priya Iyer: thanks — this was helpful. next steps?
[06:58] Samira Patel: recap: we'll (1) share partner one-pager + security pack; (2) Ethan runs perf baseline on Lumina sample; (3) Priya shares stakeholder list and timelines; (4) schedule pilot kickoff in late Feb / early March. i'll set a Doodle for availability
[07:15] [07:20] Diego Marquez: ok, thanks everyone
[07:22] Fiona Zhang: thanks
[07:23] Ethan Cole: thanks, talk soon
[07:30] Ethan Cole: ok i'm going to dig into a couple more technical items while we have time — if you want to skip, say so
[07:37] Fiona Zhang: no please go on, this is the useful part
[07:40] Ethan Cole: for the baseline we'll need a model artifact or a docker image; simplest is you share a model tar + a short prompt set. we'll run two configs: hosted with a comparable model version and a dedicated A100 instance with our continuous batching enabled. results will include p50/p95, token cost, and GPU utilization
[08:05] Diego Marquez: can you also capture cold-start times? our ephemeral containers spin up a lot during scale events
[08:11] Ethan Cole: yes, we'll capture cold-start and steady-state p95. also, we'll test with and without kv cache so you can see unit-cost delta
[08:20] Samira Patel: on the partner side, a few notes: (1) onboarding for channel requires an MSA/reseller addendum, (2) enablement deck for your sales engineers, (3) a technical integration checklist for your infra team. we'll drive those docs as immediate artifacts
[08:38] Priya Iyer: procurement will need a sample SOW for a pilot — low risk, time-boxed. can you provide that?
[08:44] Samira Patel: yes, we'll send a pilot SOW template — short, 4 weeks, acceptance criteria included
[08:50] [09:00] Fiona Zhang: one operational question — logs retention and PII handling. if a prompt contains PII, how long are transcripts stored and can we purge them programmatically
[09:09] Ethan Cole: default retention is 90 days for analytics; for private we can configure retention and offer programmatic purge endpoints, plus we support field-level redaction during ingest
[09:22] Diego Marquez: is that purge immediate or eventual consistency?
[09:26] Ethan Cole: typically eventual, but SLA'd windows can be negotiated for enterprise/policy reasons
[09:33] Samira Patel: also worth noting, for strict air-gapped deployments we can disable telemetry and only produce local logs for your compliance team
[09:42] [10:00] Diego Marquez: ok on a different note — what's the expected uplift in cost vs our internal GPU ops if we move embedding jobs to Redwood hosted. we run 6x V100s overnight already
[10:12] Ethan Cole: embeddings at scale often see cost parity or savings due to batching and optimized kernels; we'll put numbers in the benchmark spreadsheet — but it's workload dependent (seq len, model size, I/O overhead)
[10:25] Fiona Zhang: can we run a pilot only for embeddings first as a low-risk test and then expand to chat
[10:31] Samira Patel: absolutely, pilots can be segmented: embedding-only pilot first is common and helps validate cost math
[10:40] [15:00] (discussion continued - detailed engineering Q&A omitted in this transcript excerpt)
[20:10] Ethan Cole: short summary of engineering notes from the deep dive: helm charts for sidecar, example istio policies, metrics collector to Prometheus, sample DPA clauses to be prepared
[25:32] Diego Marquez: technical blocker check: if we require per-tenant encryption keys, can Redwood support per-tenant KMS keys in the private model
[25:39] Ethan Cole: yes, per-tenant KMS integration is supported in private deployments; we map keys to tenant ids and accept external HSM via standard KMS APIs
[30:05] Fiona Zhang: latency target validation — you mentioned <250ms p95 at 512 tokens, what's the tradeoff at 1024 tokens
[30:13] Ethan Cole: expect roughly linear-ish increase in per-token latency; at 1024 tokens p95 might be 1.6x the 512 figure depending on kernels; we can also recommend sequence-length aware routing and quantized variants to keep latency within SLA
[34:20] Priya Iyer: commercial — do you require minimum committed spend for channel partners to get discounts
[34:27] Samira Patel: yes typical channel tiers have banded commit thresholds; we'll include a partner pricing grid in the one-pager with thresholds and margins
[38:40] Ethan Cole: ops note — for dedicated pools we recommend a safety buffer for autoscaling (e.g., 20% spare capacity) and a fallback plan to hosted to avoid request drops during spikes
[40:10] Diego Marquez: if we go forward, we'll want a joint runbook for incident response and an escalation matrix
[40:18] Samira Patel: agreed, runbook and escalation contacts are standard for enterprise pilots; we'll include that in the SOW
[42:50] Fiona Zhang: any known limitations with the current runtime we should be aware of — long sequence memory, multi-GPU sharding, or attention optimizations missing?
[43:00] Ethan Cole: current runtime handles common model families; very large models requiring model parallelism are more complex but we have patterns for sharding; we'll surface any caveats in the perf report
[44:05] Diego Marquez: ok, sounds like enough to start. Priya, i'll follow up with details you asked for
[44:12] Priya Iyer: will do; i'll email the stakeholder list and tentative procurement window by EOW
[44:20] Samira Patel: great. closing remarks: we'll send (1) partner one-pager + partner playbook links, (2) security pack (SOC2, KMS guide), (3) SOW template and runbook draft, (4) Ethan's benchmark results next week. thanks everyone
[45:20] All: thanks, bye
